questions.question_text:
A barn is a rectangular prism topped by a half-cylinder roof.
The box is $4$ m wide and $3$ m tall, the roof is a half-cylinder of diameter $4$ m, and the barn is $12$ m long.
Find its total volume, correct to $1$ decimal place.

options.why: Used a full cylinder $\pi r^{2}h$ for the roof instead of a half-cylinder $\tfrac12\pi r^{2}h$.
Found only the rectangular box and left out the half-cylinder roof entirely.
Used the diameter $4$ as the roof radius, giving $\tfrac12\pi(4^2)(12)$ instead of $\tfrac12\pi(2^2)(12)$.

questions.solution_text:
The roof radius is $r = 2$ m.
$V_{\text{box}} = 4 \times 3 \times 12$
$= 144\text{ m}^{3}$
$V_{\text{roof}} = \frac{1}{2} \times \pi \times 2^{2} \times 12$
$= 75.3982\ldots\text{ m}^{3}$
$V = 144 + 75.3982\ldots$
$= 219.3982\ldots$
$\approx 219.4\text{ m}^{3}$

questions.question_text: A tank is a cylinder of radius $3$ m and height $5$ m standing on a rectangular prism with a square top of side $6$ m and height $2$ m. Find the total volume, correct to $1$ decimal place.

options.why: Found only the rectangular prism base and left out the cylinder on top.
Found only the cylinder and left out the rectangular prism base.
Used the side $6$ as the cylinder radius instead of $3$ when finding the cylinder volume.

questions.question_text:
A rectangular block is $8$ cm by $6$ cm by $4$ cm.
A cylindrical hole of radius $1$ cm is drilled straight through the $4$ cm thickness.
Find the volume of material remaining, correct to $1$ decimal place.

options.why: Added the cylindrical hole to the block instead of subtracting it.
Gave the full block and forgot to remove the drilled hole.
Used radius $2$ cm (the diameter) for the hole, removing four times too much.

questions.question_text:
A stepped shaft is a cylinder of radius $2$ cm and height $8$ cm sitting on a cylinder of radius $6$ cm and height $3$ cm, sharing the same axis.
Find the total volume, correct to $1$ decimal place.

options.why: Found only the larger lower cylinder and left out the smaller upper cylinder.
Found only the smaller upper cylinder and left out the larger lower cylinder.
Used radius $6$ for both cylinders instead of $2$ for the upper one.

questions.question_text:
A hollow pipe has an outside radius of $6$ cm, an inside radius of $4$ cm, and a length of $15$ cm.
Find the volume of the pipe material, correct to $1$ decimal place.

options.why: Found the outer cylinder alone without subtracting the hollow inner cylinder.
Subtracted the radii $(6-4)$ first, using $\pi(6-4)^2(15)$ instead of $\pi(6^2-4^2)(15)$.
Halved the correct answer, treating the pipe as a half-cylinder shell.

questions.question_text:
A bolt is a square-prism head on a cylindrical shaft.
The head is a square prism of side $6$ mm and thickness $3$ mm; the shaft is a cylinder of radius $2$ mm and length $10$ mm.
Find the total volume, correct to $1$ decimal place.

options.why: Found only the square-prism head and left out the cylindrical shaft.
Found only the cylindrical shaft and left out the square-prism head.
Used radius $4$ mm (the diameter) for the shaft instead of $2$ mm.

questions.question_text:
A cylindrical tank of radius $0.5\text{ m}$ and height $1.2\text{ m}$ sits on a rectangular prism $1\text{ m}$ by $1\text{ m}$ by $0.4\text{ m}$, and the whole structure holds water.
Using $1\text{ m}^{3} = 1000\text{ L}$, find its total capacity in litres, correct to $1$ decimal place.

options.why: Treated the unconverted numerical result $1.342477\ldots$ in cubic metres as litres, then rounded it to $1$ decimal place.
Found only the cylinder and left out the rectangular prism base.
Converted using $1\text{ m}^{3} = 100\text{ L}$ instead of $1\text{ m}^{3} = 1000\text{ L}$.

questions.solution_text:
$V_{\text{prism}} = 1 \times 1 \times 0.4$
$= 0.4\text{ m}^{3}$
$V_{\text{cyl}} = \pi \times 0.5^{2} \times 1.2$
$= 0.9424\ldots\text{ m}^{3}$
$V = 0.4 + 0.9424\ldots$
$= 1.3424\ldots\text{ m}^{3}$
Capacity $= (0.4 + 0.3\pi) \times 1000$
$= 1342.4777\ldots\text{ L}$
$\approx 1342.5\text{ L}$

questions.question_text:
A support column is a square prism standing on a cylindrical base.
The cylindrical base is $2\text{ m}$ in diameter and $1\text{ m}$ high.
The square prism has cross-sectional area $2\text{ m}^{2}$ and height $8\text{ m}$.
Find the total volume, in $\text{m}^{3}$, correct to $1$ decimal place.

options.why: Found only the square prism, using $2 \times 8$, and left out the cylindrical base.
Found only the cylindrical base, using $\pi \times 1^{2} \times 1$, and left out the square prism.
Used the diameter $2\text{ m}$ as the cylinder radius, giving $16 + \pi \times 2^{2} \times 1$.

questions.solution_text:
The cylindrical base has radius $1\text{ m}$.
$V_{\text{cyl}} = \pi r^{2}h$
$= \pi \times 1^{2} \times 1$
$= \pi\text{ m}^{3}$
$V_{\text{prism}} = Ah$
$= 2 \times 8$
$= 16\text{ m}^{3}$
$V = \pi + 16$
$= 19.1415\ldots$
$\approx 19.1\text{ m}^{3}$

questions.question_text:
A tunnel is $10\text{ m}$ long and has a semicircular opening $4\text{ m}$ wide.
Its concrete shell is $1\text{ m}$ thick, so the outside radius is $3\text{ m}$.
Find the volume of concrete needed, in $\text{m}^{3}$, correct to $3$ decimal places.

options.why: Found the outer half-cylinder alone, using $\frac{1}{2}\pi \times 3^{2} \times 10$, without subtracting the opening.
Used the shell thickness $1\text{ m}$ as the radius of a half-cylinder, giving $\frac{1}{2}\pi \times 1^{2} \times 10$.
Used full cylinders instead of half-cylinders, giving $\pi(3^{2} - 2^{2}) \times 10$.

questions.solution_text:
The inside radius is $2\text{ m}$.
Subtract the inner half-cylinder from the outer half-cylinder.
$V_{\text{outer}} = \frac{1}{2} \times \pi \times 3^{2} \times 10$
$= 45\pi\text{ m}^{3}$
$V_{\text{inner}} = \frac{1}{2} \times \pi \times 2^{2} \times 10$
$= 20\pi\text{ m}^{3}$
$V = 45\pi - 20\pi$
$= 25\pi$
$= 78.539816\ldots$
$\approx 78.540\text{ m}^{3}$
